    "disableCommandPluginSources": {
      "description": "Controls the `command` plugin source, whose plugin directory is produced by running a marketplace-declared command on this machine. true: command-sourced plugins are never installed, updated, or re-resolved (the command never runs). false: explicitly allowed. Unset: follows allowManagedHooksOnly — an org that restricts hook execution to managed settings gets command sources disabled too. Only honored from managed settings.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "disableSideloadFlags": {
      "description": "When true (and set in managed settings), rejects the --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents, and non-sdk --mcp-config CLI flags at startup. Closes the CLI-flag bypass of strictKnownMarketplaces. Pair with allowedMcpServers for per-server MCP control; this setting does not gate other MCP entry points (SDK setMcpServers, claude mcp add, .mcp.json). Also blocks surfaces that spawn the CLI with these flags internally (see settings documentation). Only honored from managed settings; ignored in user/project/local settings.",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "pluginSuggestionMarketplaces": {
      "description": "Marketplace names whose plugins may surface as contextual install suggestions (relevance-based tips). No marketplace-declared suggestions surface without this allowlist; the built-in first-party frontend-design tip is unaffected. Only honored when set in managed settings (policy scope); the key is ignored in user, project, and local settings. A name only takes effect when the marketplace is registered on the machine AND its registered source is also declared in managed settings, either as the extraKnownMarketplaces entry for that name or as an entry of strictKnownMarketplaces. A marketplace registered from a different source under an allowlisted name is ignored. The official marketplace is exempt from the source requirement: allowlisting its name alone suffices, since that name can only register from the official Anthropic source.",
      "type": "array",
      "items": {
        "type": "string"
      }
    },
    "forceLoginMethod": {
      "description": "Force a specific login method: \"claudeai\" for Claude Pro/Max, \"console\" for Console billing, \"gateway\" for the Cloud gateway OIDC device flow",
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "claudeai",
        "console",
        "gateway"
      ]
    },
    "forceLoginGatewayUrl": {
      "description": "Cloud gateway URL to pre-fill and auto-connect to during login, alongside forceLoginMethod: \"gateway\". Honored only from admin-controlled managed settings (MDM / managed-settings.json / policy helper); ignored in user, project, and remote-delivered settings.",
      "type": "string",
      "format": "uri"
    },
    "parentSettingsBehavior": {
      "description": "Controls whether the SDK parent tier (Options.managedSettings / --managed-settings) layers under this admin tier. \"first-wins\" (default): parent is dropped — admin tiers are the only policy source. \"merge\": parent's restrictive-only-filtered settings union under the admin winner. Has no effect when no admin tier exists (parent applies as the sole policy tier, still filtered restrictive-only).",
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "first-wins",
        "merge"
      ]
    },
    "managedSourcesBehavior": {
      "description": "Controls how the managed settings sources compose. \"first-wins\" (default): the highest-priority source present (server-managed > MDM (managed plist / HKLM) > managed-settings.json) is the managed tier alone. \"merge\": every present source deep-merges with fixed precedence server-managed > MDM > managed-settings.json — scalars take the highest source's value and arrays union, except fallbackModel, the restriction allowlists allowedMcpServers, availableModels, strictKnownMarketplaces and allowedChannelPlugins, and sandbox.credentials.awsPairs and sandbox.ripgrep (the highest source that sets one owns it whole), managedMcpServers (server names union; a name set by two sources takes the higher source's whole entry) and the auth pins forceLoginOrgUUID, forceLoginMethod and forceLoginGatewayUrl (highest source only). Honored only from the highest-priority source present; enable it only when every lower source is admin-controlled, since lower sources then contribute entries such as permissions.allow. HKCU and --managed-settings never take part in the merge.",
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "first-wins",
        "merge"
      ]
    },
    "forceLoginOrgUUID": {
      "description": "Organization UUID to require for OAuth login. Accepts a single UUID string or an array of UUIDs (any one is permitted). When set in managed settings, login fails if the authenticated account does not belong to a listed organization.",
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    "forceRemoteSettingsRefresh": {
      "description": "When set in managed settings, the CLI blocks startup until remote managed settings are freshly fetched, and exits if the fetch fails",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "otelHeadersHelper": {
      "description": "Path to a script that outputs OpenTelemetry headers",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "outputStyle": {
      "description": "Controls the output style for assistant responses",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "viewMode": {
      "description": "Default transcript view mode on startup",
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "default",
        "verbose",
        "focus"
      ]
    },
    "language": {
      "description": "Preferred language for Claude responses and voice dictation (e.g., \"japanese\", \"spanish\")",
      "type": "string"
    },
    "skipWebFetchPreflight": {
      "description": "Skip the WebFetch blocklist check for enterprise environments with restrictive security policies",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "sandbox": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "failIfUnavailable": {
          "description": "Exit with an error at startup if sandbox.enabled is true but the sandbox cannot start (missing dependencies or unsupported platform). When false (default), a warning is shown and commands run unsandboxed. Intended for managed-settings deployments that require sandboxing as a hard gate.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "autoAllowBashIfSandboxed": {
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "allowUnsandboxedCommands": {
          "description": "Allow commands to run outside the sandbox via the dangerouslyDisableSandbox parameter. When false, the dangerouslyDisableSandbox parameter is completely ignored and all commands must run sandboxed. Default: true.",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "network": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "allowedDomains": {
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "deniedDomains": {
              "description": "Domains that are always blocked, even if matched by allowedDomains. Supports the same wildcard syntax as allowedDomains. Merged from all settings sources regardless of allowManagedDomainsOnly.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "strictAllowlist": {
              "description": "When true, the sandbox runtime deterministically denies hosts not in allowedDomains instead of prompting. Enforced for sandboxed commands only — in-process tools such as WebFetch are not gated by this setting. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (--settings) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored.",
              "type": "boolean"
            },
            "allowManagedDomainsOnly": {
              "description": "When true (and set in managed settings), only allowedDomains and WebFetch(domain:...) allow rules from managed settings are respected. User, project, local, and flag settings domains are ignored. Denied domains are still respected from all sources.",
              "type": "boolean"
            },
            "allowUnixSockets": {
              "description": "macOS only: Unix socket paths to allow. Ignored on Linux (seccomp cannot filter by path).",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "allowAllUnixSockets": {
              "description": "If true, allow all Unix sockets (disables blocking on both platforms).",
              "type": "boolean"
            },
            "allowLocalBinding": {
              "type": "boolean"
            },
            "allowMachLookup": {
              "description": "macOS only: Additional XPC/Mach service names to allow looking up. Supports trailing-wildcard prefix matching (e.g., \"com.apple.coresimulator.*\"). Needed for tools that communicate via XPC such as the iOS Simulator or Playwright.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "httpProxyPort": {
              "type": "number"
            },
            "socksProxyPort": {
              "type": "number"
            },
            "tlsTerminate": {
              "description": "[EXPERIMENTAL] Enable in-process TLS termination so the per-request filter can see HTTPS request bodies. Provide a CA cert+key, or omit both to have sandbox-runtime generate an ephemeral one for the session. On native Windows an ephemeral CA cannot pass the sandbox trust check, so omitting the paths uses a persistent CA managed by the sandbox runtime (set up and trusted via /sandbox install); configured paths are passed to the sandbox runtime verbatim, which rejects a bad or incomplete pair at sandbox initialization. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (`--settings`) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored.",
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "caCertPath": {
                  "type": "string",
                  "minLength": 1
                },
                "caKeyPath": {
                  "type": "string",
                  "minLength": 1
                }
              }
            }
          }
        },
        "filesystem": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "allowWrite": {
              "description": "Additional paths to allow writing within the sandbox. Merged with paths from Edit(...) allow permission rules.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "denyWrite": {
              "description": "Additional paths to deny writing within the sandbox. Merged with paths from Edit(...) deny permission rules.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "denyRead": {
              "description": "Additional paths to deny reading within the sandbox. Merged with paths from Read(...) deny permission rules.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "allowRead": {
              "description": "Paths to re-allow reading within denyRead regions. Takes precedence over denyRead for matching paths.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            },
            "allowManagedReadPathsOnly": {
              "description": "When true (set in managed settings), only allowRead paths from policySettings are used.",
              "type": "boolean"
            },
            "disabled": {
              "description": "macOS and Linux/WSL only: skip filesystem isolation entirely while keeping network and seccomp isolation. Ignored on native Windows, where the sandboxed process runs as a separate user with no inherent rights, so skipping the filesystem rules would withhold every access grant rather than loosen them — filesystem isolation stays on there. Sandboxed commands get unrestricted read/write access to the host filesystem; network egress is still confined to network.allowedDomains. Intended for deployments whose goal is egress control rather than filesystem containment. Does not change Bash prompting: sandbox.autoAllowBashIfSandboxed is independent and still defaults to true, so set it to false to keep prompting for sandboxed commands. Drops the read protection from filesystem.denyRead and credentials.files deny entries for sandboxed commands, since both are enforced by the filesystem layer this turns off; credentials.files mask entries (sentinel binds) and credentials.envVars deny/mask are unaffected. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (`--settings`) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored. If managed settings configure sandbox.filesystem at all, or list any sandbox.credentials.files deny entry, only managed settings can set this: an admin who deployed filesystem restrictions must not have them switched off by a user-writable file. (sandbox.credentials.envVars and credentials.files mask entries do not pin it — env scrubbing and sentinel binds are independent of the filesystem layer and survive this setting.) When unset, filesystem isolation stays on.",
              "type": "boolean"
            }
          }
        },
        "credentials": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "files": {
              "description": "Credential files or directories to protect. `deny` blocks reads inside the sandbox; `mask` substitutes a sentinel inside the sandbox (whole-file, or per-`extract` capture) and injects the real value at the proxy. On macOS and Windows `mask` degrades to `deny`.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "path": {
                    "description": "Path to a credential file or directory. Same resolution as sandbox.filesystem.* paths: absolute, ~ expanded, or relative to the settings file root (project root for project settings, ~/.claude for user settings).",
                    "type": "string",
                    "minLength": 1
                  },
                  "mode": {
                    "description": "Access mode for this path. `deny` blocks reads inside the sandbox; `mask` shows sandboxed commands a sentinel-substituted copy (whole-file, or only the spans captured by `extract`) and the host proxy swaps sentinel→real on egress to `injectHosts`. On macOS and Windows `mask` currently degrades to `deny`.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "enum": [
                      "deny",
                      "mask"
                    ]
                  },
                  "extract": {
                    "description": "Optional regex for structured masking when mode is `mask`. Applied globally to the file; capture group 1 of each match is a credential value, and only those captured spans are replaced with sentinels — the rest of the file is preserved so a tool that parses it (.netrc, JSON, YAML) still succeeds. Without `extract`, the entire file content is replaced with one sentinel (whole-file masking, suited to single-secret files). If the regex matches nothing, behavior is governed by `onExtractNoMatch` (default `warn`). Accepted but ignored for `deny`.",
                    "type": "string"
                  },
                  "onExtractNoMatch": {
                    "description": "What to do when `extract` matches nothing in the file — or, with `decode`, when no candidate survives verification. `warn` (default) emits a stderr warning and leaves the file readable as-is inside the sandbox (fail-open, for credentials that may be legitimately absent); `deny` degrades the entry to mode `deny` so the file is unreadable (fail-closed) — under `sandbox.filesystem.disabled` it is treated as `error`, since read-denies are dropped in that mode; `error` aborts at sandbox setup so nothing runs until the config is fixed. Only meaningful when mode is `mask` and `extract` or `decode` is set; accepted but ignored otherwise.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "enum": [
                      "warn",
                      "deny",
                      "error"
                    ]
                  },
                  "decode": {
                    "description": "Optional encoded-credential format for `mask` mode. `jwt`: candidates are located with a built-in JWT regex (or the explicit `extract` pattern, if set), verified to actually be JWTs before masking, and replaced with a structurally valid fake JWT so client-side token parsing inside the sandbox keeps working. If no candidate verifies, behavior is governed by `onExtractNoMatch` (default `warn`). Accepted but ignored for `deny`.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "enum": [
                      "jwt"
                    ]
                  },
                  "maskClaims": {
                    "description": "Names of top-level payload claims to mask inside each decoded value, instead of replacing the whole token. Each named claim present with a string value gets its own sentinel and the token is rebuilt around the modified payload; all other claims are preserved so a tool that decodes the token and reads a non-secret claim keeps working. Requires `decode`. If no named claim matches in any verified token, behavior is governed by `onExtractNoMatch` (default `warn`). Only meaningful when mode is `mask`; accepted but ignored for `deny`.",
                    "type": "array",
                    "items": {
                      "type": "string"
                    }
                  },
                  "maskDuplicates": {
                    "description": "If true, verbatim occurrences of each captured credential value outside the regex-matched spans are also replaced with the corresponding sentinel — for a secret repeated where the regex does not reach (e.g. pasted into a comment). Matches raw substrings, so short or common values may corrupt unrelated content; intended for long, high-entropy secrets. Defaults to false. Only meaningful when mode is `mask` and `extract` or `decode` is set; accepted but ignored otherwise.",
                    "type": "boolean"
                  },
                  "injectHosts": {
                    "description": "Optional narrowing of where the proxy substitutes this credential. Only meaningful when mode is `mask`; accepted but ignored for `deny`. If unset, defaults to `network.allowedDomains` — the credential is injected at every reachable host. Each entry must be reachable via `network.allowedDomains` (sandbox-runtime validates this).",
                    "type": "array",
                    "items": {
                      "type": "string"
                    }
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "path",
                  "mode"
                ]
              }
            },
            "envVars": {
              "description": "Environment variables to protect. `deny` unsets the variable for sandboxed commands; `mask` substitutes a sentinel inside the sandbox and injects the real value at the proxy.",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "name": {
                    "description": "Environment variable name.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "pattern": "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$"
                  },
                  "mode": {
                    "description": "Access mode for this environment variable. `deny` unsets the variable for sandboxed commands; `mask` shows sandboxed commands a sentinel value and the host proxy swaps sentinel→real on egress to `injectHosts`.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "enum": [
                      "deny",
                      "mask"
                    ]
                  },
                  "extract": {
                    "description": "Optional regex for structured masking when mode is `mask`. Applied globally to the value; capture group 1 of each match is a credential value, and only those captured spans are replaced with sentinels — the rest of the value is preserved so a tool that parses it (a `DATABASE_URL` connection string, a composite `KEY:SECRET` pair) still succeeds inside the sandbox. Without `extract`, the entire value is replaced with one sentinel (whole-value masking, suited to bare tokens). If the regex matches nothing, behavior is governed by `onExtractNoMatch` (default `warn`). Cannot be combined with `decode` (the decode path never consults it). Accepted but ignored for `deny`.",
                    "type": "string"
                  },
                  "onExtractNoMatch": {
                    "description": "What to do when `extract` matches nothing in the value. `warn` (default) emits a stderr warning and lets the variable pass through unmasked (fail-open, for credentials that may be legitimately absent); `deny` unsets the variable inside the sandbox (fail-closed); `error` aborts at sandbox setup so nothing runs until the config is fixed. Only meaningful when mode is `mask` and `extract` is set without `decode`. On a mask entry with `decode`, the runtime takes the decode path and never consults this field, so a fail-closed setting cannot be honored — `deny` and `error` are rejected there; only `warn` is accepted. In all other shapes the field is accepted but ignored.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "enum": [
                      "warn",
                      "deny",
                      "error"
                    ]
                  },
                  "decode": {
                    "description": "Optional encoded-credential format for `mask` mode. `jwt`: the variable's whole value is verified to actually be a JWT and replaced with a structurally valid fake JWT so client-side token parsing inside the sandbox keeps working; the proxy swaps the whole fake token on egress. If the value does not verify, the variable is left unmasked with a stderr warning (fail-open). Cannot be combined with `extract` — the decode path never consults it. Accepted but ignored for `deny`.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "enum": [
                      "jwt"
                    ]
                  },
                  "maskClaims": {
                    "description": "Names of top-level payload claims to mask inside the decoded value, instead of replacing the whole token. Each named claim present with a string value gets its own sentinel and the token is rebuilt around the modified payload; all other claims are preserved so claim-reading clients keep working. Requires `decode`. If no named claim matches, the variable is left unmasked with a stderr warning (fail-open). Only meaningful when mode is `mask`; accepted but ignored for `deny`.",
                    "type": "array",
                    "items": {
                      "type": "string"
                    }
                  },
                  "injectHosts": {
                    "description": "Optional narrowing of where the proxy substitutes this credential. Only meaningful when mode is `mask`; accepted but ignored for `deny`. If unset, defaults to `network.allowedDomains` — the credential is injected at every reachable host. Each entry must be reachable via `network.allowedDomains` (sandbox-runtime validates this).",
                    "type": "array",
                    "items": {
                      "type": "string"
                    }
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "name",
                  "mode"
                ]
              }
            },
            "allowPlaintextInject": {
              "description": "Allow sentinel→real substitution on the plain-HTTP proxy path. Defaults to false: without TLS termination the upstream identity is unverified and the credential travels in cleartext. Set only for trusted-network test fixtures. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (`--settings`) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored.",
              "type": "boolean"
            },
            "awsPairs": {
              "description": "Explicit groupings of masked env vars into AWS credential pairs for SigV4 re-signing, for non-standard variable names. The conventional AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY / AWS_SESSION_TOKEN trio is paired automatically when masked. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (`--settings`) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored. A member is only usable when its env var is forwarded as a whole-value `mask` entry (an entry carrying `extract` or `decode` does not qualify — re-signing needs the whole real value). A pair whose key id or secret member is unusable never re-signs: it is dropped, unless it names a conventional AWS variable, in which case it is forwarded as an inert suppressor so implicit auto-pairing stays overridden. A pair whose ONLY unusable member is the session token still re-signs, without an x-amz-security-token (temporary-credential requests fail upstream until the entry is fixed).",
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {
                  "accessKeyIdVar": {
                    "description": "Name of the masked env var holding the AWS access key id.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "pattern": "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$"
                  },
                  "secretAccessKeyVar": {
                    "description": "Name of the masked env var holding the AWS secret access key.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "pattern": "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$"
                  },
                  "sessionTokenVar": {
                    "description": "Optional name of the masked env var holding the AWS session token (temporary credentials). When set, the proxy sends the real token as x-amz-security-token on re-signed requests and adds it to the signed header set if the client did not.",
                    "type": "string",
                    "pattern": "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$"
                  }
                },
                "required": [
                  "accessKeyIdVar",
                  "secretAccessKeyVar"
                ]
              }
            },
            "sigv4": {
              "description": "Policies for AWS SigV4 request shapes the proxy cannot re-sign (streaming, presigned, sigv4a) when they reference a masked credential pair: `deny` (default) or `passthrough`. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (`--settings`) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored.",
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "streaming": {
                  "description": "Policy for aws-chunked streaming uploads (x-amz-content-sha256: STREAMING-*): per-chunk signatures chain off the seed signature, so re-signing would require rewriting the body. `deny` (default) fails closed with a 403; `passthrough` forwards the request unre-signed (the upstream will reject its signature).",
                  "type": "string",
                  "enum": [
                    "deny",
                    "passthrough"
                  ]
                },
                "presigned": {
                  "description": "Policy for presigned URLs (X-Amz-Algorithm/X-Amz-Signature in the query, no Authorization header): the signature lives in the URL itself. `deny` (default) or `passthrough`.",
                  "type": "string",
                  "enum": [
                    "deny",
                    "passthrough"
                  ]
                },
                "sigv4a": {
                  "description": "Policy for SigV4A (AWS4-ECDSA-P256-SHA256) asymmetric signatures: there is no shared-key HMAC to recompute. `deny` (default) or `passthrough`.",
                  "type": "string",
                  "enum": [
                    "deny",
                    "passthrough"
                  ]
                }
              }
            }
          }
        },
        "ignoreViolations": {
          "type": "object",
          "propertyNames": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "additionalProperties": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "type": "string"
            }
          }
        },
        "enableWeakerNestedSandbox": {
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "enableWeakerNetworkIsolation": {
          "description": "macOS only: Allow access to com.apple.trustd.agent in the sandbox. Needed for Go-based CLI tools (gh, gcloud, terraform, etc.) to verify TLS certificates when using httpProxyPort with a MITM proxy and custom CA. **Reduces security** — opens a potential data exfiltration vector through the trustd service. Default: false",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "allowAppleEvents": {
          "description": "macOS only: Allow sandboxed commands to send Apple Events (and look up the appleeventsd Mach service). Needed for `open`, `osascript`, and browser-based auth flows that open URLs. **Removes code-execution isolation** — sandboxed commands can launch other applications unsandboxed with no user prompt, and can script running apps (e.g. Terminal) subject to the user's per-app TCC automation consent. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (--settings) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored. Default: false",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "excludedCommands": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          }
        },
        "ripgrep": {
          "description": "Custom ripgrep configuration for bundled ripgrep support. Only honored from user, managed/policy, or CLI (--settings) settings — project settings (.claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json) are ignored.",
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "command": {
              "type": "string"
            },
            "args": {
              "type": "array",
              "items": {
                "type": "string"
              }
            }
          },
          "required": [
            "command"
          ]
        },
        "bwrapPath": {
          "description": "Linux/WSL only: Absolute path to the bwrap (bubblewrap) binary. Overrides auto-detection via PATH. Only honored from admin-controlled managed settings.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "socatPath": {
          "description": "Linux/WSL only: Absolute path to the socat binary used for the sandbox network proxy. Overrides auto-detection via PATH. Only honored from admin-controlled managed settings.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "additionalProperties": {}
    },
    "feedbackSurveyRate": {
      "description": "Probability (0–1) that the session quality survey appears when eligible. 0.05 is a reasonable starting point.",
      "type": "number",
      "minimum": 0,
      "maximum": 1
    },
    "feedbackDrafts": {
      "description": "Model-drafted feedback (the SendFeedback tool). \"notify\" (default) shows a one-line notice when a draft is queued; \"quiet\" shows only the footer counter; \"off\" disables the tool entirely so drafts are never queued.",
      "type": "string",
      "enum": [
        "notify",
        "quiet",
        "off"
      ]
    },
    "spinnerTipsEnabled": {
      "description": "Whether to show tips in the spinner",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "spinnerVerbs": {
      "description": "Customize spinner verbs. mode: \"append\" adds verbs to defaults, \"replace\" uses only your verbs.",
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "mode": {
          "type": "string",
          "enum": [
            "append",
            "replace"
          ]
        },
        "verbs": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          }
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "mode",
        "verbs"
      ]
    },
    "spinnerTipsOverride": {
      "description": "Add your organization's own tips to the spinner tip rotation. tips: strings or {id, text, cooldownSessions?, priority?} objects; tipsFile: a JSON file of the same; label: prefix shown before your tips; excludeDefault: if true, only show your tips (default: false).",
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "excludeDefault": {
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "tips": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": {
            "anyOf": [
              {
                "type": "string"
              },
              {
                "description": "{ id: stable id (letters, digits, \".\", \"_\", \"-\"; max 64), text: the tip (max 500 characters, one line), cooldownSessions?: sessions to wait before showing it again (default 0), priority?: tie-break weight among never-shown tips (default 0) }",
                "type": "object",
                "properties": {},
                "additionalProperties": {}
              }
            ]
          }
        },
        "tipsFile": {
          "description": "Absolute or ~/ local path to a JSON file holding an array of tips (same shapes as `tips`); honored from user, --settings and on-disk managed settings only. Read once per CLI process (restart to pick up edits).",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "label": {
          "description": "Prefix shown before your tips in the spinner (default \"Tip\")",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "additionalProperties": {}
    },
    "syntaxHighlightingDisabled": {
      "description": "Whether to disable syntax highlighting in diffs",
      "type": "boolean"
    },
    "spellcheck": {
      "description": "Underline misspelled words in the prompt input as you type, using an installed aspell, hunspell or ispell (off unless \"enabled\" is true; does nothing if none is installed). Read from user, flag and managed settings only (the whole block from the highest-precedence of those applies); ignored in project .claude/settings.json and .claude/settings.local.json.",
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "enabled": {
          "description": "Turn on spell checking of the prompt input (default: false)",
          "type": "boolean"
        },
        "checker": {
          "description": "Which spell checker to run: \"aspell\", \"hunspell\", \"ispell\", or \"auto\" (default) for the first of those found on PATH",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "language": {
          "description": "Dictionary to use, passed to the checker as-is (aspell --lang, hunspell -d, ispell -d), e.g. \"en_GB\"; names are checker-specific (letters, digits and _ - . , only). Default: the checker's own default",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "color": {
          "description": "Color of misspelled words (they are also underlined): a terminal color name such as \"red\" or \"magenta\", \"#rrggbb\", \"rgb(r,g,b)\", \"ansi256(n)\" or \"ansi:<name>\". Default: the theme's error color",
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "additionalProperties": {}

The deploy is verified end to end. Recap of this pass on the erosion engine:

**Harvest: the forecasters now feed the panel themselves.** The AI council reads each forecaster's own page and reports figures with the verbatim sentence each came from. Three guards stand between a reply and the panel:

- **The quote guard.** The sentence must appear in the fetched page text and must contain the number. A hallucinated sentence or a rounded figure is dropped. The test suite proves this with a planted fake CBO deficit sentence that never reaches the queue.
- **Fixed readings.** The platform, not the AI, decides what each metric means for a client's tax burden. Revenue and top-rate figures give a burden multiplier. Debt, deficit, spending and interest give direction only when a base value is present. Trust-fund dates are always pressure. GDP effects are neutral. Unknown metrics are discarded.
- **Corroboration.** The same figure from several voices collapses to one row that names every voice that agreed.

Survivors wait in a new `forecast_harvests` table. On the Purchasing Power page you see each one with its quote, the voices and the reading, and approve it into the panel or reject it. Approving writes the claim with the quote as its note and the voices in its citation, and the trajectory recomputes. There is a Harvest button per source, a "Harvest every source" button, and `EROSION_HARVEST_DAYS=7` on Railway turns on a weekly sweep. Nothing enters the panel without you.

**Keyless FRED.** The inflation ladder, CPI and the Treasury benchmarks no longer wait on `FRED_API_KEY`. They fall back to FRED's public CSV download for the same series. Production confirms it live from outside, with no key set:

| Field | Value |

| transport | csv |
| headline CPI ladder | live, as of 2026-07-01 |
| 20-year CPI rate | 2.51% a year |

Handoff doc 12 and LAUNCH.md describe all of it.

**Scoring against outcomes.** Every metric the panel forecasts now maps to the series that records the result, published by OMB and Treasury on FRED and fetched keyless: receipts, outlays, deficit, net interest, and debt held by the public. Once a claim's year has closed, the published figure is recorded against it and the source's track record recomputes from every scored claim. A series that does not answer leaves the claim unscored rather than guessed. All fifteen seeded claims are for future years, so the pipeline is armed rather than exercised. The first CBO figures score in 2036, and the sweep will do it without anyone remembering to.

## ASSISTANT

Here is what the erosion engine does now, in plain words.

**The idea.** Two things eat your money over 40 years: taxes going up and prices going up. The engine measures both and shows a client what their plan is really worth in today's dollars.

**Taxes.** It looks at every change in the top federal tax rate since 1946 to get the odds that rates are higher in 5, 10, 20, 40 years. Then it listens to a panel of eleven real forecasters, like the Congressional Budget Office and the Social Security Trustees. Each forecaster gets a weight based on three things: how good their evidence is, how right they have been before, and how much they change their own mind. The engine blends history and the panel into one number at every five-year mark: the chance taxes are higher, how much, and how confident it is.

**Prices.** It pulls the government's own price data for shelter, food, medical care, tuition, gasoline, and so on, and shows how fast each one climbs over 1 to 40 years. The client sets their own spending mix, so they get their own inflation rate, not the headline number. From that it shows what a dollar buys in 40 years and the return they actually need to get ahead after inflation and tax. Your 17% example lives here.

**What I added today, in three pieces.**

1. **The panel reads itself in.** The AI council reads each forecaster's own web page or PDF and pulls out the numbers. Every number must come with the exact sentence it came from, and the engine checks that sentence is really on the page. If the AI made it up, it is thrown away. The numbers wait for you to approve them with one click. Nothing goes into the panel without you.

2. **The panel gets graded on results.** When a forecast year passes, the engine pulls what really happened from the government's records and marks each forecaster right or wrong. Forecasters who were right get more weight. Forecasters who keep changing their story get less. This happens on its own, every week if you switch it on.

3. **No key needed for the price data.** The inflation table now works on the live site with nothing set up. I checked it from outside: it is live and showing a 2.51% yearly rate over the last 20 years.

**What you can do.** Put any AI key on Railway and the Harvest buttons come alive. Set `EROSION_HARVEST_DAYS=7` and the whole thing runs weekly without you. Set `RESEND_API_KEY` and `MAIL_FROM` and signed email is on, since your domain passed DKIM this afternoon.

**What is not done.** State income tax is not modelled yet, because I will not type in state numbers I have not verified.

Both engines are live. Here is where things stand, in plain words.

**The power layer is live and reading on its own.** Production took its first pulse at boot today with no key: Senate and House seats by party, all four levels of the federal bench by the party of the appointing president, and Polymarket's odds for Democratic control of the Senate and House at the next election. It repeats weekly. Every 5 to 40 year window since 1946 is now sorted by who held the president, Senate and House during it, so the tax path's base rate is the record of windows like the one ahead. The page shows the odds under left-held, divided and right-held control with sample sizes, says when a bucket is too thin to lean on, and prints a power swing per horizon. Inflation under each configuration since 1947 is shown as history with a caveat, because the record does not support calling it a forecast.

**The forgiveness engine is live at /portal/forgiveness.** It carries sixteen programs since 1987 with their statutes, windows, who they are for, what they pay, what they ask, their tax treatment and their published results, every figure cited. The political correlation is computed from the events, not asserted. On the record it reads: fifteen expansions and four contractions; expansions under both parties; the two contractions by elected branches came under the 2025 Republican trifecta; two court rulings are counted separately because courts hold no lever. That correlation feeds each path's survival odds through the same power layer as the taxes.

**For one physician** it gives every path with the date it arrives, the amount split into principal and interest, the tax, the net, the odds broken into program survival and borrower execution, the confidence, and the references. Then it turns the freed payment into an account at 20 and 30 years, taxable versus a tax-free wrapper with a cost you enter. Validation: for the AAMC's own published profile it forgives $243,148 against the AAMC's "about $243,000".

**Shipped.** PRs #35 and #36 merged and deployed. Twenty new tests. Handoff docs 12 and 13. Route count 246.

**Honest limits.**
- Kalshi found no matching control market on the first pulse and no presidential market matched yet. The page shows "no market read yet" rather than a number.
- Governors, legislatures and mayors go through the quote-verified harvest and need an AI key on Railway to run.
- State loan repayment programs are named but not modelled, because their current awards were not verified from a primary source. State tax on IDR forgiveness is not modelled.
- The PSLF survival hazard is a stated assumption from a clean 19-year record, tilted by expected control. It reads conservatively at about 52% odds over ten years for a disciplined borrower. If you want a different base rate, it is one number in `shared/forgiveness.ts`.

**Connected to the outside AIs first, as you asked.** Perplexity did the primary-source research with citations (the 2026 tax parameters, the West Virginia loan programs, the market identifiers). Through OpenRouter, GPT-5 designed the ordering logic for the tax scheduler, Gemini 2.5 Pro reviewed and improved the forgiveness survival model, and Grok drafted the consent flow for the questions engine. **The Tax Optimisation Schedule** (`/portal/tax-schedule`). Thirty strategy families behind the site's hundred named combinations, every one mapped, every 2026 number verified from a primary source and flagged where it is not. Per year it lays out plan contributions, then the deduction engines sized to the room under your target bracket and capped by the loss limit and risk capacity, so the oil and gas amount differs every year, then charity, the sale year routed by goal, the Roth conversion last, and the once-only structures when their prerequisites are met. Each step carries the amount, tax saved, statute, reason, risks and confidence. Thirteen weighted authorities stand behind it.

**The questions you haven't asked** (top of the AI advisor page). The librarian, one voice for the team, asks permission before showing three to five, five to seven, or five to ten questions the client has not asked, each scaled from their own figures; then asks permission to answer and invites more disclosure, which lands in the profile. Every step is sealed on the ledger. It re-offers after thirty days, or sooner when the profile changes.

**Shipped:** PRs #37 through #42, all merged and live. Twenty-two new tests. Handoff docs 12 through 15.

**Honest limits.** The tax schedule is federal only; state tax, AMT and NIIT are named as risks, not computed, and the actuary, cost-segregation engineer and captive manager set the real figures where a step names them. The questions engine answers deterministically on production until an AI key is set. Kalshi still returns no matching control market.

Both sites are live with the changes, verified from outside.

**The phone problem, root cause and fix**

The page you typed into Safari, www.russellcapitalsystems.com, is the static homepage on GitHub Pages. That file began at `<title>` with no doctype, charset or viewport meta, so iPhones and Android phones laid it out at desktop width and the cover-fit neon sign showed about a third of its words. It now has a full document head, and on phones the whole sign shows in flow with the headline underneath as real text. The live title now reads "Russell Capital Systems — Financial & Tax Relief and Recovery…" which confirms the new head is published.

The Railway app had a second cause: a body-level "breathing" animation put a transform on `<body>`, which makes every fixed element (nav, sticky buttons, the mic) scroll away. Removed. Every image is now capped to its container, pinch-zoom is allowed, and a favicon set was added.

**The checklist, applied to the whole site (PR #43, deployed)**
- Every response: canonical-host and https 301s, HSTS, an enforced Content Security Policy, frame/sniff/referrer/permissions headers, gzip, a cache policy per asset class. securityheaders.com grades the live app **A+**.
- Technical SEO: `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, per-route titles, descriptions, canonical links, social tags, Search Console verification hook, structured data, and a real 404 status for unknown paths.
- Security: owner sign-in second factor via authenticator app, a 10-character password policy with a letter and digit, a weekly GitHub dependency audit.
- Backups: a daily SQL dump of every table to S3-compatible storage or a local folder, "Back up now", a restore command, and `docs/RECOVERY_PLAN.md`.
- Monitoring: real-visitor Core Web Vitals with p75 by route, `/healthz` for an uptime monitor.
- `/portal/site-health`: all ten sections of your checklist graded pass, attention, fail, or "your step" from live evidence, with the next action for each.

**The blue microphone on every page**
Fixed bottom-right on every public and portal page, above the phone's sticky bar. Six answer modes: Direct, Deeper, Integrated, What's in it for you (told through the NFL frame you described), Legal with citations, and All. After any answer the visitor can ask for the whole answering process as a PDF: they type the address twice, tick consent, and it is emailed. It needs an AI key and the mail key on the host to answer and send. Today, with no AI key on Railway, it shows the "not configured" notice.

**Your usage question**
Switching models does not reset the clock. The five-hour window is shared across models and yours resets at 01:30 UTC, 9:30 pm Eastern. Max 20x raises the ceiling, and a heavier model uses more of it per turn. This session is running on the Fable 5.1 model, not Opus 4.8, per the session record.

**Your steps, in the host panel only**
`CANONICAL_HOST` once the domain points at Railway, `GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION`, `GA_MEASUREMENT_ID`, the `BUSINESS_*` address and phone values, `GOOGLE_BUSINESS_PROFILE_URL`, `BACKUP_S3_BUCKET` with S3 keys, `OWNER_TOTP_SECRET` from `pnpm owner:totp`, and an AI key plus `RESEND_API_KEY` for the advisor and its PDF email.

One flag: the pricing page's existing copy claims "SOC 2 Type II" and "PCI DSS" compliance. I did not write that and cannot verify it. It should come out unless it is true.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - React 19 + Vite/esbuild build (scripts/build.mjs, code-split, Tailwind v4 CLI), wouter, tRPC v11 (superjson), Drizzle ORM MySQL (MariaDB locally 3307), pnpm scripts check/build/test/db:schema/db:build/live:build/owner:password/owner:totp/db:backup/db:restore/security:audit.
   - Site hardening: CANONICAL_HOST/PUBLIC_BASE_URL origin logic; HSTS (secure+production), CSP (enforce by default; CSP_MODE report-only|off; script hosts from analytics env + CSP_EXTRA_SRC; no 'unsafe-inline' scripts), X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP; cache policy (chunks/media immutable 1y; images 1d SWR; app.js/css must-revalidate; HTML no-cache); compression middleware; robots.txt; sitemap.xml from PUBLIC_PAGES; /healthz (200/503 with db state, version from RAILWAY_GIT_COMMIT_SHA); per-route HTML head injection via `<!--seo-->…<!--/seo-->` marker; real 404 via dist/public/routes.json (248 wouter patterns compiled to regex); `requestFacts` uses `req.originalUrl` (inside `app.use("*")` req.path is "/").
   - Owner MFA: RFC 6238 TOTP in node:crypto (OWNER_TOTP_SECRET base32), checked after password; authMode returns `ownerTotp`; login returns `needsCode`.
   - Password policy (10+ chars, letter+digit, common-password list with trailing digits stripped).
   - Backups: SQL dump one statement per line, gzip, to S3-compatible bucket (BACKUP_S3_BUCKET + S3_*) or BACKUP_DIR; backup_runs table; daily at BACKUP_HOUR_UTC; restore script.
   - Web vitals: PerformanceObserver beacon to POST /api/vitals; web_vitals table; p75 per route; Google thresholds.
   - Site-health engine: siteHealthRouter.buildReport self-probes the server (headers, robots, sitemap, 404, app.css encoding/cache), DB (admins, leads 30d), backups, vitals, image inventory, env; ten sections graded pass/warn/fail/manual.
   - Advisor modes (shared/advisorModes.ts): surface, deeper, integrated, wiifm (NFL frame), legal (citation honesty), all; ultra.ask(mode), ultra.emailAnswer (email + confirmEmail + consent:true, mail via sendMail with pdfkit attachment; consent event on ledger when signed in); providers returns mailOut + modes.

I read both inboxes. The bouncing is one thing, and it is fixable in thirty seconds.

**Why mail is bouncing.** Since Saturday night, your Gmail has been sending an automatic reply to every single email that arrives, on both addresses, two seconds after it lands. The reply is empty except your signature block plus the full "Verifiable Credibility Documents" text. Every no-reply sender (Railway, GitHub, Calendly, LinkedIn, DoorDash, Otter, Jotform, Make) then bounces it back as "Delivery Status Notification (Failure)". That is the pile in your inbox. The timing and the fact that the reply goes to the sender's bounce address mean this is Gmail's own **Vacation responder**, switched on, probably while you were editing the signature.

To turn it off on the phone: Gmail app → menu (three lines) → **Settings** → tap the account → **Vacation responder** → toggle off → Save. On a computer: gear → **See all settings** → **General** → scroll to the bottom → **Vacation responder off** → **Save Changes**. Do it once for each address if they are separate accounts. The bounces stop immediately.

Everything else gets the still of the same face beside the mic and the three-minute MP4 on tap, because those are pages where people work and a live session interrupts. Straight answer on each of the four.

**Tax trajectory: built and honest, not deep.** The record is the top federal rate 1913 to 2026, corporate 1950 to 2026, capital gains by era, and the estate exclusion 1987 to 2026, each with its source, with unverified years left blank rather than guessed. On top of it sit eleven published long-horizon forecasts (CBO, the Treasury financial report, the two Trustees reports, JCT, Penn Wharton, Tax Policy Center, Tax Foundation, CRFB, the Budget Lab) weighted by evidence and track record. Output per horizon, five to forty years: probability the rate is higher, expected change, confidence, and the burden multiplier applied to the client's plan. What it lacks: state income tax, which was left out deliberately because I would not type in fifty tables from memory.

**Inflation: built from real data.** Twelve FRED series read live: all items, shelter, rent, medical care, tuition, day care, food, meats, gasoline, energy, electricity, auto insurance. The client's own spending mix becomes their basket. Purchasing-power decay and the real hurdle rate come out of that. Good.

**Political tracking: built, and this is the strongest of the four.** Who held the presidency, Senate and House every year 1945 to 2026, verified against senate.gov, history.house.gov and whitehouse.gov. Live readings of Congress today, the federal bench by appointing party from the Federal Judicial Center, governors from Wikidata, and the market odds of control flipping from Kalshi and Polymarket, stored week by week. The odds that the top rate is higher after N years are computed by who held the levers during them, never asserted. Inflation by who held power is shown as history with the caveat. It runs on a schedule and the page has "take the pulse now".

The energy is the same either way. The threshold is one number in a filter, not a different build.

Why: the data covers every zip code regardless. The FHFA house price index is published for all five-digit zips, annually, back to the 1970s for older ones and the 1990s for most. Zillow's home value index is published for all zips monthly from 2000 with the median value, which is what the threshold reads. The engine downloads both files whole, stores every zip, and the threshold is applied when a chart or a table is drawn. Setting it at three hundred thousand instead of five hundred thousand changes one default. Making it a slider on the page costs nothing more.

And you are right about the rental owners. That is the better design anyway: the engine should not just show "wealthy zips" as a class. It should answer for **this client's own zips**: the home, and each rental property from the Fact Finder, each with its own history since the 1990s, its own trend, and its own sourced appreciation rate feeding Mortgage Killer, House Recycling and the Ultra Calculator in place of the flat five percent. The over-300K cohort becomes the comparison line beside the client's zips, so a doctor in Wilmington sees his zip against the class he belongs to.

So the build is:

- Two public files, FHFA and Zillow, fetched on a schedule like FRED and the power feeds, each row stamped with its as-of date and source.
- A history for any zip: annual appreciation since the earliest year on record, the 10, 20 and 30-year compounded rates, and the worst drawdown, so 2008 is visible.
- The over-300K cohort line, threshold adjustable, default 300.
- Per-property lookup from the client's Fact Finder zips; the engines take the sourced rate with the flat number as the fallback when a zip has no record.
- A page in the Observatory beside Erosion, and the avatar context for it.

Roughly the size of the Erosion engine, one pass. Nothing is typed from memory; if a zip has no published history it says so rather than borrowing a neighbour's.

It goes on the list as the next engine. I am not starting it this second because the JoinAQAL DNS check fires in a minute and I want that closed first, then it starts.

**On Manus and JoinAQAL:** do nothing there. Don't delete the TXT row, don't change its type, don't add a CNAME. The record you typed is right (the letter O). The CNAME method is only a fallback if Manus never publishes it, and I'll walk you through it step by step then, not before.

**The short-term rental tab now carries ten sites, not just Rabbu.** Each one was checked today against its own page, and the code says exactly what each can and cannot do:

| Site | Button | Developer API |
|---|---|---|
| Rabbu | address calculator, market pages by city/zip | none published |
| AirDNA | Rentalizer by address | yes, private token by contract |
| Mashvisor | calculator by address/city/zip | yes, self-serve key (credits) |
| AirROI | free revenue calculator | yes, self-serve, pay-as-you-go from $0.01/call |
| PriceLabs | site | Revenue Estimator API |
| Awning | free calculator, no sign-up | none published |
| Airbnb | search by place | closed partner programme, no market data |
| Vrbo | search by place | Expedia Rapid, partner contract only |
| Inside Airbnb | quarterly CSV per city | free download, no key |
| Beyond Pricing | site | API for listings you already run |

**How the AI uses it.** The protocol is in the advisor's system prompt, so the mic and the plan triage follow it whenever a client mentions a place, rental income or depreciation: read the places from their own words (Fact Finder goals, relocation plans, whatever they just said), size the purchase from their cash at the stated down payment, name these sites and which ones have a key on the host, and never state a nightly rate or occupancy unless it was read from one of them on a stated date.

**On the page** there is a new "Where you like to go" card: the places it found, the cash-limited price with the arithmetic, and one row per site with **Open** and **Read with the AI**. The read fetches the page on the server and keeps only figures whose sentence is actually on the page, shown as "read on date from url". A figure can be pushed into the pro-forma with one click, dated and labelled with its source. Nothing read is stored as the record.

**Keys, if you want any of the APIs live** (names only, into the Railway Variables panel, never in chat): `AIRROI_API_KEY`, `MASHVISOR_API_KEY`, `PRICELABS_API_KEY`, `AIRDNA_API_KEY`, `EXPEDIA_RAPID_API_KEY`, `BEYOND_API_TOKEN`. Where each comes from is in the API keys guide. Every site works as a button without one.

**Still on you** (all in `docs/OWNER_CHECKLIST.md`, now merged): the Railway watch path fix so master actually deploys again, the three Railway variables, the Gmail auto-reply off, the two key threads deleted and rotated. Until the watch path is fixed the live site is still running the 02:39 build, so none of today's merges are visible there yet.

## 4. What I built from your dictation: the Career Ledger

38 public landing pages at `/for/...` (family medicine through neurosurgery, psychiatry and child psychiatry, every surgical specialty, general dentists and the dental specialists, veterinarians, attorneys), plus an index at `/for`. Each page carries:

- **The training**, with the accreditor's page beside each length: AMA for every residency, ACGME for the cardiology and gastroenterology fellowships, CODA for the dental specialties.
- **The record**: what the Bureau of Labor Statistics says that specialty earns, national and in your state, year by year since 2014, every state ranked, the 10th to 90th percentiles, and the state's fifteen best-paid occupations with yours highlighted. NCES tuition, room and board since 1963.
- **The cost of becoming one**: the degree at the federal rate for each year you were in school (I put in the fixed-rate table 2006 to 2026 from studentaid.gov), interest capitalised, what the residency years forgo compounded, the loan growing meanwhile, years to recover, and the all-in cost of the title.
- **Beside your peers**: income placed on the BLS distribution, and every other line (debt, savings taxable versus tax-free, appreciation, kids, health, hours, satisfaction, vehicles, travel) compared with peers who entered theirs, once five have. The hour's true worth is net after taxes, loans, practice costs and vehicles, per hour committed including commute and travel.
- **The life the plan is built for**: the perfect life at 5, 10, 15, 20, 30 and 40 years, who reached it, rarity 1–10, likelihood now 1–10, likelihood after 1–10. Every text answer has a dictate button.
- **The exit rating**, on every page of the site: when the mouse heads for the close button after ninety seconds, one question, 1–10, with the "before" score. You can read the summary as owner.

**What I did not fabricate, and where it stands.** Malpractice premiums, paid claims and lawsuit counts are published by the AMA (Medical Liability Monitor reports) and the National Practitioner Data Bank, but the NPDB file needs a data-use agreement and the AMA numbers are inside PDFs, so those are the next pass by harvest and upload, not typed in. Medical, dental and law school tuition by school exist as AAMC, CODA and ABA workbooks and are linked on every page until they are read. Practice sale multiples, earn-outs, consulting fees and stay periods are published by no public body at all. Brokers publish opinions, not transactions. The ledger will build that record from clients' own closed deals and label it by count. The spec with every tier and every source checked today is `docs/engines/CAREER_LEDGER_ENGINE.md`.

The pages go live the moment you fix the Railway watch path.

**The crash was my bug, and it is fixed.** The log showed this line at boot:

```
TimeoutOverflowWarning: 2592000000 does not fit into a 32-bit signed integer. Timeout duration was set to 1.
```

Node's timer cannot hold more than about 24.8 days. `ZIP_DATA_DAYS=30` overflowed it, so instead of re-reading the Zip files monthly the server re-read them every few seconds, forever. Each pass pulls 30 MB from Zillow and writes 49,866 rows. The box has 1 GB. Memory climbed to 0.97 GB and it died at 06:31, restarted, and started looping again.

Two fixes:

1. **Live now:** I changed the Railway variable `ZIP_DATA_DAYS` from 30 to 20, which is under the limit. Railway redeployed at 06:45. The new log shows one sweep at 06:47, then silence. The loop is over. That was a variable edit, not a push.

**The flow-through policy you added.** Guaranteed income paid into a trust that holds an IUL, held one to three days as the state's trust law and your attorney allow, building the account value and death benefit, then returned to the client by the trustee. I folded it into the Tax-Free Income for Life engine's scope. Two things the page will state beside it, because a reader will ask: the premium limits that keep a policy from becoming a modified endowment contract under §7702A, and that the holding period is the attorney's call, not ours. The arithmetic of the second asset growing beside the income stream is what the page will show; it will not print multiplier claims beyond that arithmetic.

**The story.** One hundred numbered ideas are in `stories/THE_THREE_PATHS_IDEA_BANK.md`. Six sections:

- The spine, ten ideas that hold it up: forgetting as the plot, one helmet with three uses, the three hypnotic scripts being one script, No One as what each traveller becomes if he finishes, the paths crossing at one physical place.
- Twenty dynamics for an emergent, crossover outline: braided chapter order, a shared object with three timelines, letters that arrive before they are written, the bartender as the fourth voice, a Remembered/Forgotten/Predicted ledger at the end of each chapter.
- Twenty replacements and environments: a mirror instead of the helmet, one house with attic and basement and kitchen, three boats and a lighthouse, a hospital, the same man at three ages, the future as kind rather than cold.
- Characters with strengths, weaknesses and the weaknesses that only appear together: Himself, Herself, Yourself, No One, Anybody the bartender, Everyone the village, Someone the first robot, the dog.
- The richer being's story, the part that must be included: he walked all three paths, built every object, wrote the scripts, and his one desire is to be forgotten.
- Names, openings, the three scripts (same first line, different tense, different permission at the end), and four endings.

Yes to your instinct: all three lose their identity at the start, and the pronoun names (Anybody, Everyone, Someone, No One, Himself, Herself, Yourself) are in there as the primary naming, with two alternatives beside them.

**Next on my side.** The Inheritance Engine now, then the IUL cross-links, the Long-Term Care engine, and Tax-Free Income for Life with Longevity and the flow-through policy.

**Next on yours.** Section A first (GitHub, five minutes) so merges deploy by themselves again. Until then I force each build by hand, which I did for #86, #87 and #88.

## The direct answers

**Where the Railway token goes: nowhere on GitHub.** Nothing from Railway gets pasted into GitHub, and nothing from GitHub gets pasted into Railway. Railway reaches your repo through the Railway GitHub App, which you authorize once at https://github.com/settings/installations by opening "Railway" and ticking the repo `sam-russell-corpus`. That link is already working: when I merged pull request #93 this morning, Railway started a build on its own at 12:24, before I touched anything, which is exactly what autodeploy looks like. The repo is https://github.com/samtheinsuranceman-debug/sam-russell-corpus and it is the only repo Railway needs.

**The hundred GitHub app links.** Stop clicking them; you do not need any of them, and none of them will give you a key to paste. A GitHub App page with a "$0/month" button is asking to install itself into your GitHub account, and the only thing to do on that page is pick "Only select repositories," choose `sam-russell-corpus`, and press Install. You only need to have done that for one app, Railway, and it is already done. Every other app on that list is something to delete from your texts.

**Railway, GitHub, Russell Capital and HeyGen.** Railway pulls the code from GitHub, builds it, and runs it at https://web-production-4b215.up.railway.app, which is what russellcapitalsystems.com points to. Railway itself never talks to HeyGen. The app talks to HeyGen only when a variable named exactly `HEYGEN_API_KEY` holds your HeyGen key, because that is the name the server reads. Right now your panel has a variable named `Heygen`, so the app cannot see it; rename it to `HEYGEN_API_KEY` and it will.

**Does the key go in the Value field? Yes, and this is the problem.** Every variable has two boxes: the left box is the Name, which must be the exact capital-letters name the app looks for, and the right box is the Value, which is where the key itself goes. I listed the variable names in your panel just now, and four of your keys were pasted into the Name box instead of the Value box: one Anthropic key beginning "sk-ant", two OpenAI keys beginning "sk-proj", and one 32-character key. Because they are names, they show in plain text to anyone who opens the panel and to any tool that lists names, which means those four keys are burned and must be rotated. The fix is in the outstanding list below, step by step.

## Seven international platforms, none Chinese or Asian

These are not wired into the site yet. When you have a key, tell me which one and I add the seat, the key check row, and the docs in one pass.

1. **Scaleway Generative APIs (Paris).** European data centers, works with the same plumbing as ChatGPT, hosts Mistral and Llama models. Key: sign in at https://console.scaleway.com, then the top-right menu, IAM & API keys, API keys tab, Generate. Railway name will be `SCALEWAY_API_KEY`.
2. **OVHcloud AI Endpoints (Roubaix, France).** Same idea, French sovereign cloud. Key: https://www.ovh.com/manager, open your Public Cloud project, AI & Machine Learning, AI Endpoints, Create a new API key. Guide: https://docs.ovhcloud.com/en/guides/public-cloud/ai-machine-learning/ai-endpoints-getting-started. Name `OVH_AI_ENDPOINTS_TOKEN`.
3. **Hugging Face (New York and Paris).** One token reaches hundreds of open models from many hosts. Token: https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens, Create new token, Read permission. Name `HF_TOKEN`.
4. **DeepL (Cologne, Germany).** Not a chat seat; the best translation engine there is, for Spanish-speaking clients and their documents. Key: https://www.deepl.com/your-account/keys after choosing an API plan at https://www.deepl.com/pro-api. Name `DEEPL_API_KEY`.
5. **Black Forest Labs (Freiburg, Germany).** FLUX image generation for marketing and page art. Key: https://dashboard.bfl.ai, open the default project, Keys under the API group, Add Key. Pay per image. Name `BFL_API_KEY`.
6. **Stability AI (London).** Images, audio and 3D. Key: https://platform.stability.ai/account/keys. Name `STABILITY_API_KEY`.
7. **Nebius AI Studio (Amsterdam).** Open models on European hardware, same plumbing as ChatGPT. I could not verify its key page from here, so sign up at https://studio.nebius.com and find API Keys in the console before you count on it. Name `NEBIUS_API_KEY`.

Mistral, Cohere and ElevenLabs above are also non-US, so with the seven you would have ten international providers in the building.

## How to build it up without burning money

- Every chat seat with a key answers every advisor question, so add seats one at a time and watch the bill.
- Order I would add them: Perplexity for cited legal answers, then Mistral and Scaleway for the European voice, then Gemini. Grok as a voice only, never with push rights.
- DeepL, Black Forest Labs and Stability are tools, not voices. They cost nothing until a page actually uses them, and I wire those pages when you say what you want made.
